name: GNS Page and Site Tracker
author: gsmith6673

sections.description:
Most traffic tools are written for engineers. This one is written for the rest of us.

When you install GNS Page and Site Tracker, you don’t need Google to get started. Click “Start tracking,” and the plugin begins counting page views and link clicks on your site right away. If you want more detail and a longer history, connect Google Analytics through the free Site Kit by Google plugin, and the same dashboard shows those numbers too.

What you can see

  • Page views. How many times each page was viewed, with your most-viewed pages first.
  • Link clicks. Which links people clicked, which page they clicked from, and whether the link was in your menu or somewhere else on the page.
  • Device type. Whether visitors were on a phone, tablet, or computer.
  • Focus page. Pick one page you care about, such as a new post, and check on it each time you visit. The plugin compares it with the period before, so you can see whether it is growing.

Two ways to count

  • Built-in counter. This works on its own with no Google account. It starts counting the day you turn it on and does not include earlier visits.
  • Google Analytics (optional). If Site Kit by Google is installed and connected to Google Analytics, you can see your Google page views from before you installed this plugin. On the Google tab, link clicks are counted for Amazon links (amzn.to and amazon.com) only.

What it does not count

  • Visits while you or another user are signed in to WordPress.
  • Common search engine bots and crawlers. No bot filter is perfect, so some automated traffic may still be counted.

Privacy

The Built-in counter stores daily totals only: the page, the link clicked (without anything after a “?” in the address), whether the link was in a menu, the date, and a general device type (phone, tablet, computer, or unknown).

It does not store IP addresses, names, or email addresses. It does not set cookies or track individual visitors from page to page. All counts stay in your own WordPress database. The plugin does not send the Built-in counter’s data anywhere.

If you use the optional Google Analytics tab, those numbers come from your own Google Analytics account through Site Kit by Google. Google’s own privacy terms apply to that data.

You may still want to mention in your site’s privacy policy that you count page views and link clicks.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “GNS Page and Site Tracker,” and click Install, then Activate.
  2. Open Page & Site Tracker in the left-hand menu.
  3. Click Start tracking. Counting begins right away.
  4. Optional: to see your Google Analytics history, install and connect Site Kit by Google, then open the Google Analytics tab.
sections.faq:
Do I need Google Analytics?

No. The Built-in counter works on its own. Google Analytics is optional and adds history from before you installed this plugin.

Why don’t the Built-in counter and Google Analytics show the same numbers?

They count separately. Ad blockers and some privacy settings stop Google from counting, so the Built-in counter usually shows more. The two may also use different time zones. Neither one is wrong. They are two separate counts.

Why are my Google link clicks blank or zero?

Google counts link clicks only when Enhanced Measurement (outbound clicks) is turned on in your Google Analytics settings. Also, the Google tab counts Amazon links only. The Built-in counter counts clicks on all web links.

Why doesn’t Google show today’s numbers?

Google can take a day or two to finish counting, so the Google tab shows completed days only. Recent numbers may still change.

Why are my own visits missing?

Visits while signed in to WordPress are left out on purpose, so your own checking and editing don’t inflate the numbers.

What does “Unknown” mean under “By device”?

The visitor’s browser didn’t say what kind of device it was.

What happens to my data if I turn the plugin off or delete it?

Deactivating the plugin keeps all of your counts, so you can turn it back on later and pick up where you left off. Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen removes its counts, its settings, and any saved focus pages from your WordPress database.
sections.changelog:
0.11.3

  • Plainer wording throughout the dashboard.
  • Added short explanations of the Focus page, why the two counts differ, Google link-click settings, and the “Unknown” device type.
  • All dashboard text can now be translated.
  • Google Analytics now counts clicks on www.amazon.com links, not only amazon.com and amzn.to.
  • Fixed: the Built-in counter recorded nothing on sites whose address includes a port number, such as local test sites.
  • Deleting the plugin now removes its data. Deactivating it still keeps your counts.
